paper_title: Near-Optimal Dynamic Steiner Spanners for Constant-Curvature Spaces
classifications: Theory of computation → Approximation algorithms analysis
Theory of computation → Nearest neighbor algorithms
statement: Let R be a fixed d-dimensional Riemannian manifold (of non-constant curvature). Can one construct a Steiner spanner for any set of n points in R that has size O eR (ε(1−d)/2 n)? Can we get a polynomial dependence on the genus g for Steiner spanners on (constantcurvature) surfaces? Is there a near-linear size ε-additive Steiner spanner in hyperbolic space that is dynamic? Can we remove the α(n) factor in its edge count? Can we strengthen Lemma 12, for example by getting a smaller number of trees or already getting a Steiner (1 + ε)-spanner with O(dn) edges at distances o( 1ε log 1ε )?
